title: Memory sets records while the grid gets locked up
intro: Micron's record quarter and a steep 2027 HBM price outlook put memory at the center of the week, while Constellation signed 4.3 GW of nuclear and PJM supply with Google and Amazon. Anthropic's IPO filing reportedly shows $518B of compute commitments, and Broadcom is lining up financing for OpenAI's custom chips.
movers_note: First snapshot. Week-over-week moves appear after the next refresh.

items.headline: Micron posts a record $54.2B fiscal Q4 and guides to $61.5B
items.summary: Fiscal Q4 revenue rose about 379% year over year at roughly 87% gross margin, bringing fiscal 2026 sales to $133.2B. The next-quarter guide implies about 13% sequential growth, and management credited long-term customer agreements for the durability.

items.headline: Google signs 3.6 GW with Constellation, including 890 MW of nuclear uprates
items.summary: A 20-year deal backs about $4.3B of upgrades across 11 reactors in Illinois, New Jersey and Pennsylvania, alongside a 15-year agreement for 2.7 GW from existing PJM plants. Constellation shares rose by double digits on the news.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO prospectus reportedly shows $518B of compute commitments
items.summary: Reuters' review of the confidential filing puts about 80% of the spend as non-cancellable, including roughly $161B of Broadcom equipment leases, $111B with Google, $110B with Amazon and $31B with Microsoft. The company is reportedly targeting a valuation near $2T.

items.headline: Broadcom reportedly arranging $50B+ of financing for OpenAI's custom inference chips
items.summary: The WSJ reports Apollo and Blackstone are among lenders weighing participation, with nothing yet committed. It would extend the AI XPV platform Broadcom launched with the same firms in June, whose $35B first tranche was earmarked for Anthropic capacity.

items.headline: TrendForce raises its 2027 HBM outlook: blended prices up 121%
items.summary: The revision rests on tight advanced-node and wafer capacity, slow yield gains on next-generation stacks, a larger HBM4 mix and an HBM4e ramp in late 2027. GPU and ASIC makers are weighing 8-Hi stacks over 12-Hi to stretch supply.

items.headline: Musk confirms Terafab talks with TSMC; 2027 price increases expected
items.summary: SpaceX is discussing a fab tie-up in which TSMC would own and run a Texas plant with equity or wafer commitments from the partner; nothing is final. Taiwanese press expects 2027 increases of 5-10% on advanced nodes and 10-15% on advanced packaging. TSMC reports Q3 on Oct 15.

items.headline: Foxconn's September revenue tops NT$1 trillion for the first time
items.summary: Hon Hai booked a record NT$1.16T in September (up about 38% year over year), and Q3 revenue grew about 47% on AI server demand, beating estimates. It expects AI-related growth to continue this quarter.

items.headline: Amazon signs a 20-year, 690 MW nuclear PPA with Constellation at Calvert Cliffs
items.summary: The agreement includes about 190 MW of new capacity targeted for 2030-2032 and more than $3B of plant investment, plus a retail supply deal for Amazon's PJM operations.

items.headline: Tencent reportedly leases ~100,000 NVIDIA chips from Oracle in Southeast Asia for $7B
items.summary: Per the FT, the five-year deal gives Tencent access to hardware Chinese firms cannot buy directly. US rules restrict direct purchases but not offshore rentals, a gap the arrangement highlights.

items.headline: CoreWeave opens Vera Rubin NVL72 to customers
items.summary: CoreWeave received its first production racks in early September and stood up a cluster for Cognition within days. Cognition reports up to 4.8x the token throughput of GB200 NVL72 on its inference workload.

items.headline: Arista unveils Etherlink SU-144 Ethernet scale-up racks for 144 accelerators
items.summary: The open rack-scale design links up to 144 accelerators in one hop and scales to 1,024 across racks, supporting ESUN, NVLink Fusion and PCIe; AMD, Arm, Broadcom and Qualcomm are named partners. Demo at OCP Summit Oct 12-15; no ship date yet.

items.headline: Study counts 343 immersion DUV tools in China after $13B+ of ASML purchases
items.summary: A Centre for Technology and Statecraft study says about 270 of them are ASML NXT:1980i systems, with more than $13B spent in 2024-25. It argues mature-node tools can be repurposed for advanced lines, strengthening the case for tighter export limits.
